chunks.text: Foreword BIS being the National Standards Body of India has the onus of leading the Standardization activities in the nation, BIS has taken up a monumental task of mapping of applicable Indian Standards to government schemes/missions run by various ministries. Extensive brainstorming exercise was done by officers of Standardization and Certification departments to map more than 3200 Indian Standards towards 75 government schemes/missions panning across
chunks.title: Foreword

chunks.text:
29 Ministries/Departments of Government of India. Following key advantages are envisaged through this exercise:
Products procured by Central/State Government Departments for implementation of schemes are of right quality and adhere to Indian Standards. Wherever there are certain processes/services involved, the executive departments follow right code of practices. In case of certain products/processes/services for which Indian Standards are not available; such gap areas are identified in timely manner and respective technical committees can take up the matter for formulation of standards on such areas. Standards and quality culture is imbibed in central/state government departments across all levels, as adherence to Indian Standards fosters a culture of quality and reliability within government departments. For future schemes/missions government departments can proactively get involved with BIS for providing the necessary assistance pertaining to standardization needs related to upcoming schemes/missions. This will assist Ministries in preparing Annual Work Programme for Standardization. The Indian Standards for each scheme mission have been classified into two broad categories:
Product Standards Other than Product Standards For each of these broad categories we have further identified:
Standards Available Standards Under Development Areas Identified for Standardization in Future Furthermore, mandatory standards under Quality Control Order (QCO) have been marked in dark shades. With the mapping exercise BIS aims to contribute further towards a more effective and efficient implementation of various schemes/missions run by government and to imbibe quality culture across all levels where these schemes are making an impact. This booklet includes standards relevant to respective Ministry/Department and is a part of Schemes through Standards document available on BIS website.

various schemes/missions run by government and to imbibe quality culture across all levels where these schemes

through following link:

Section 3: Mapping of Scheme/Missions Digital India Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology About the Scheme/Mission Government has launched the Digital India programme with the vision of transforming India into a digitally empowered society and a knowledge—based economy, by ensuring digital access, digital inclusion, digital empowerment and bridging the digital divide. The programme is centred on three key vision areas, namely digital infrastructure as a core utility to every citizen, governance and services on demand, and digital empowerment of citizens. sections.text: Foreword BIS being the National Standards Body of India has the onus of leading the Standardization activities in the nation, BIS has taken up a monumental task of mapping of applicable Indian Standards to government schemes/missions run by various ministries. Extensive brainstorming exercise was done by officers of Standardization and Certification departments to map more than 3200 Indian Standards towards 75 government schemes/missions panning across
sections.title: Document preamble

sections.text:
29 Ministries/Departments of Government of India.
Following key advantages are envisaged through this exercise:
Products procured by Central/State Government Departments for implementation of schemes are of right quality and adhere to Indian Standards.
Wherever there are certain processes/services involved, the executive departments follow right code of practices.
In case of certain products/processes/services for which Indian Standards are not available; such gap areas are identified in timely manner and respective technical committees can take up the matter for formulation of standards on such areas.
Standards and quality culture is imbibed in central/state government departments across all levels, as adherence to Indian Standards fosters a culture of quality and reliability within government departments.
For future schemes/missions government departments can proactively get involved with BIS for providing the necessary assistance pertaining to standardization needs related to upcoming schemes/missions.
This will assist Ministries in preparing Annual Work Programme for Standardization.
The Indian Standards for each scheme mission have been classified into two broad categories:
Product Standards Other than Product Standards For each of these broad categories we have further identified:
Standards Available Standards Under Development Areas Identified for Standardization in Future Furthermore, mandatory standards under Quality Control Order (QCO) have been marked in dark shades.
With the mapping exercise BIS aims to contribute further towards a more effective and efficient implementation of various schemes/missions run by government and to imbibe quality culture across all levels where these schemes are making an impact.
This booklet includes standards relevant to respective Ministry/Department and is a part of Schemes through Standards document available on BIS website. Complete Schemes through Standards document can be accessed through following link:
https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Mapping-of-Schemes_Missions-of-Government-of-India.pdf The document is of evolutionary nature and same has been prepared as discussion document. BIS will keep on updating this document based on inputs received from Central/State Ministries and Departments.
Indian Standards are readily available for download on BIS website under “Know Your Standards” tab and can be accessed through link or QR code mentioned below:
https://www.services.bis.gov.in/php/BIS_2.0/bisconnect/knowyourstandards/indian_standards/isdetails Indian Standards can be searched by any of the following ways:
a) By IS Number b) By Keyword/Standard Title

Section 3: Mapping of Scheme/Missions Digital India Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology About the Scheme/Mission Government has launched the Digital India programme with the vision of transforming India into a digitally empowered society and a knowledge—based economy, by ensuring digital access, digital inclusion, digital empowerment and bridging the digital divide. The programme is centred on three key vision areas, namely digital infrastructure as a core utility to every citizen, governance and services on demand, and digital empowerment of citizens. The overall goal is to ensure that digital technologies improve the life of every citizen, expand India’s digital economy, and creating investment and employment opportunities and create digital technological capabilities in India.
